deploy-bot: Deploy started: release=v3.4.2 canary=10% region=us-west-2 image=runtime:2026-03-15T12:00Z :rocket:

oncall-liz: got paged by PagerDuty — saw alerts for canary 10% about 12:02 UTC, high p95 latency and some 5xxs

kai: confirming metrics — p95 spiked from ~120ms -> ~950ms at 12:03, error rate (5xx) jumped to 0.8% on canary cluster

megan: logs show an uptick in kernel fallback events and repeated KV cache misses for long-tail requests, looks like eviction thrash

sre-aaron: @kai can you paste the dashboard link? also any change in request mix (seq len)?

kai: dashboard https://dash.internal/r/abc123 — seeing shift: proportion of short chats (seq < 32) increased along with some streaming requests that keep KV warm but small token windows

eng-runtime-julie: this build includes a new memory allocator tweak + kernel select heuristic tuned for long sequences. Might be picking wrong kernels for short sequences, causing frequent fallback and cache invalidation

oncall-liz: incident-bot: paging impact: "canary: increased latency & partial throughput degradation, customers affected: small number of high-QPS customers in us-west-2; severity: Sev-2"

cs-ella: I'm seeing two customers reporting timeouts in support queue, low volume but high business impact. Notifying account reps now.

megan: stack snippet from canary node 7:```
W runtime/kernel_selector.cpp:235 fallback to cpu kernel for op attention_v2 (reason: quant mismatch)
E runtime/kv_cache.cpp:412 eviction thrash, reinsert failure
```

eng-runtime-julie: that "quant mismatch" string points to a heuristic that prefers int8 kernels for certain ops; if sequence lengths skew low it can be worse. Also allocator change may reduce soft capacity causing faster KV evictions

sre-aaron: mitigation options: 1) flip kill-switch to pin kernel selection back to stable; 2) rollback canary to previous image; 3) increase canary batch timeout/disable continuous batching for canary. Thoughts?

kai: we can test kernel pin quickly via feature-flag. That avoids full rollback and should stop fallback churn. Rollback is safest for customer impact though slower

oncall-liz: we need to act fast — customer timeouts visible. recommend kill-switch then monitor 5min window. If not stable, rollback.

megan: I can push kill-switch now: /ff set runtime.kernel_fallback_control=stable-legacy for cluster canary-us-west-2

deploy-bot: Feature flag update request received by ops-cluster-controller

ops-bot: applied feature flag runtime.kernel_fallback_control=stable-legacy to canary-us-west-2 @12:07:23 UTC :white_check_mark:

kai: immediately seeing error rate drop to 0.15% and p95 dropping to ~180ms at 12:09 — much better but still above baseline 120ms

cs-ella: customer replies: "latency seems better, thanks" from one affected customer. Another reporting reduced timeouts

eng-runtime-julie: good sign. The allocator tweak may still reduce cache capacity by design. Suggest also temporarily increasing KV cache soft limit on canary nodes to avoid evictions while we validate code change

megan: increasing kv_cache.soft_limit from 80% -> 95% on canary nodes now via runtime-config API

deploy-bot: runtime-config update applied to 6 nodes in canary-us-west-2 @12:12:01 UTC

kai: p95 now at ~140ms and errors ~0.05% — nearly baseline

oncall-liz: switching incident status to "mitigated" and starting customer impact log. Will keep monitoring and plan rollback if any regression returns

sre-aaron: action items: - eng-runtime to revert kernel heuristic in next hotfix OR add fallback backstop - performance team to add synthetic short-seq load to canary test - ops to document FF flip process - CS to follow up with affected customers and log timeline

eng-runtime-julie: I'll open a PR to revert heuristic and add a metric gate for quantized kernel selection. Assigning to @megan for review.

cs-ella: I'll triage CS tickets and tag impacted accounts, prepping comms for SLA owners

oncall-liz: handing off to daytime oncall @kai for extended monitoring — if we see recurrence escalate back to Rav (pager)

kai: taking handoff. Monitoring at 30s cadence.

megan: quick note: we should run a canary for the revert behind feature flag so we can re-enable perf gains for long sequences once stable

sre-aaron: agreed. We should schedule postmortem and link signal graphs. Tentative postmortem owner: eng-runtime-julie. Meeting at 15:00 UTC today

oncall-liz: closing the immediate page. if anything flares, page again. great cross-team response. :trophy:

eng-runtime-julie: adding logs/metrics snapshot to incident ticket: https://tickets.internal/INC-9876

cs-ella: CS notes added to ticket. Customer impact: two accounts, transient timeouts, no data loss.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket INC-9876 updated, status=mitigated

oncall-liz: last check 12:18 UTC — all good. last message timestamp 2151234860

kai: leaving a short recap to include in postmortem: cause = kernel-selection heuristic + allocator change interacting with short-sequence traffic -> KV cache thrash -> kernel fallbacks -> latency spike; mitigation = kernel-selection FF flip + increased cache limit; followups = revert heuristic, add short-seq canary tests, docs for FF kill-switch procedure

sre-aaron: nice work everyone.
